lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Animal Groups
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about animal groups from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about an animal group.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about animal groups.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions about animal groups.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about animal groups.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about an animal at home.

lessons.title: Counting and Sorting Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and sort animals into groups, recording totals.
success_criteria: I can count animals in a group.
I can record the total.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sorting animal counters into groups (mammal/bird/fish) and counting each group.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort and count animal counters into groups, recording totals.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record sorting and counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.plenary: Class total count for each animal group.
lessons.home_link: Sort toy animals into groups at home.

lessons.title: What Is a Mammal?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features common to mammals.
success_criteria: I can name a mammal.
I can describe one mammal feature (fur, live young, breathe air).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss common mammal features (fur/hair, breathe air, most give birth to live young, feed milk to young).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort animal picture cards into mammal/not mammal, recording reasoning.
key_questions: Why is this animal a mammal?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for tricky examples (e.g. bats, whales)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note classification understanding — evidence for SCI.ANI.

lessons.title: Writing Animal Fact Sentences
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences about an animal group.
success_criteria: I can write a fact about an animal group.
I can use a capital letter and full stop.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a factual sentence about mammals.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 factual sentences about mammals.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about mammals.

lessons.title: Using Tally Charts: Animal Survey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to record data using a simple tally chart.
success_criteria: I can make a tally mark.
I can count tally marks to find a total.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss favourite animals as a quick vote.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model recording a survey using tally marks and counting totals.
lessons.independent_task: Children conduct a simple class survey (favourite animal group) using tally marks.
key_questions: How do you make a tally mark for 5?

differentiation.greater_depth: Complete the survey and identify the most popular group independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early data handling skill using tally charts — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Do a simple tally survey with your family (e.g. favourite fruit).

lessons.title: What Is a Bird?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features common to birds.
success_criteria: I can name a bird.
I can describe one bird feature (feathers, beak, lay eggs).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss common bird features (feathers, beaks, wings, lay eggs), noting not all birds fly.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort animal picture cards into bird/not bird, recording reasoning.
key_questions: Why is this animal a bird?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for tricky examples (e.g. penguins, ostriches)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note classification understanding — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Look for birds outside and name one you see.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Animal Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read animal-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read animal words.
I can read a sentence about animals.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending animal-themed words (e.g. 'bird', 'fish', 'wing').
lessons.independent_task: Children read animal-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading animal words over the week.

lessons.title: Making a Simple Pictogram
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent data in a simple pictogram.
success_criteria: I can draw a picture for each item.
I can say which group has the most.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the tally survey from Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model converting tally data into a simple pictogram using one picture per item.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a pictogram from the animal survey data, answering simple questions about it.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record data representation skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Make a simple pictogram of something at home (e.g. toys by colour).

lessons.title: What Is a Fish? (Recap and Extend)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare fish, mammal, and bird features.
success_criteria: I can name a fish feature.
I can compare it to a mammal or bird feature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap fish features and compare directly to mammal and bird features studied this week.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a comparison table for mammal, bird, and fish features.
key_questions: How is a fish different from a bird?
What do mammals, birds and fish all need?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add additional features and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note classification and comparison skill across three animal groups — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap the three animal groups compared.
lessons.home_link: Sort toy/picture animals into mammal, bird, fish groups at home.

lessons.title: Animal Group Guessing Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to ask yes/no questions to identify an animal group.
success_criteria: I can ask a yes/no question.
I can guess the animal group.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models asking yes/no questions about a hidden animal.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss effective yes/no questions to narrow down an animal group.
lessons.independent_task: Children play a guessing game in pairs, asking yes/no questions to identify a partner's chosen animal group.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note questioning skill and animal group knowledge — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Play a yes/no animal guessing game with your family.

lessons.title: Animal Group Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using an animal context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using an animal group context (e.g. birds flying away).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve animal-themed word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up an animal word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Animal Habitats
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to match animals to their habitat.
success_criteria: I can name an animal's habitat.
I can say why it lives there.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the concept of habitat and match a few animals to habitats (forest, ocean, desert).
lessons.independent_task: Children match animal picture cards to habitat pictures, explaining reasoning.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of habitat suitability — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the habitat of a pet or local animal.

lessons.title: Animal Groups Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about animal groups.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's animal group learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about animal groups, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on animal groups you learned about.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Data Handling and Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply tally, pictogram, and word problem skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can read a tally/pictogram.
I can solve a word problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of tallying, pictograms, and word problems.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: data handling, word problems.
key_questions: How did you solve this problem?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 21 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising word problems over the weekend.

lessons.title: Animal Groups Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about mammals, birds and fish learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a feature of each animal group.
I can name an example of each.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering mammals, birds, fish, and habitats.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Animal Groups' display.
key_questions: What group is this animal in?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain classification reasoning in detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note animal classification understanding progress — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's animal groups learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about animal groups with your family.
